BiblicalUsage: The word is simply 'we', and it appears over a hundred times — Joseph's brothers tell the governor, 'We are all one man's sons; we are true men,' and the psalm says, 'we are the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand.' It is the word a people uses about itself, whether they are defending their honesty or confessing whose they are.
TheologicalSignificance: A pronoun carries no theology of its own; its weight is belonging — 'we are the people of his pasture' is the confession the whole Bible keeps making.
